channel.title: Farsçadan (English)
channel.description: AI-assisted English translations of selected stories from Iran's Persian-language press. Every story notes the outlet's political orientation.

item.title: Trump rejected nuclear weapons but kept 'mother of all bombs' on the table
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Trump said he won't use nuclear weapons against Iran but didn't rule out MOABs against nuclear facilities; Iran responded with a counter-threat. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Supertanker hit in the Strait of Hormuz: Sepah says mine, India claims bullet strike
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: A supertanker carrying over 2 million barrels of crude was damaged in the Strait; Sepah said mine, India claimed projectile hit. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: CENTCOM claims blockade is 'impenetrable,' Reuters reports Iran selling LPG and jet fuel
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: CENTCOM commander says Iran's $25 billion oil exports are blocked; Reuters reports Iran selling LPG and jet fuel by tanker loads. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Azerbaijan's hijab ban: Ankara backs away from criticism, Kayhan calls it a 'threat'
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Turkish Foreign Minister Fidan and former PM Yildirim retracted criticism of Azerbaijan's hijab ban; Kayhan framed it as a "threat." (Source: Kayhan)

item.title: Shot in the head at a Dey protest, Peyman Kadiri dies nine months later
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Dey uprising protester Peyman Kadiri, allegedly shot in the head by security forces, died after nine months unable to exit a coma. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Turkish parties oppose Mecca Pact: 'Don't drag Ankara into Yemen war'
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Turkish political parties warned that the Mecca Pact signed with Saudi Arabia could draw Turkey into Yemen's conflict. (Source: ISNA)

item.title: Iran's top diplomat: We are seriously considering withdrawing from the NPT
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: A senior Iranian diplomat said Tehran is evaluating withdrawal from the nuclear nonproliferation treaty as a serious option. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: U.S. Treasury adds 16 people and 10 institutions linked to Iran to sanctions list
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The U.S. Treasury Department targeted Iran's networks for currency and oil revenue, adding 16 individuals and numerous institutions to sanctions. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Lebanon's Central Bank revoked Bank Saderat Iran's operating license
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: According to Bloomberg, Lebanon's Central Bank revoked Bank Saderat Iran's license in line with regional restrictions. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: 14 political prisoners at Evin: Government intensifies crackdown ahead of anticipated protests
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Fourteen political prisoners at Evin Prison warned that the government intensified repression in anticipation of public protests. (Source: Iran International)

item.title: Container ship with 2,500+ boxes sinks in Hormuz after hitting mine
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: IRGC says a container vessel hit a mine in Hormuz and sank; Singapore and Reuters sources call it an attack and report multiple vessel incidents. (Source: Hamshahri)

item.title: Riyadh airport emptied: Missile strikes Jeddah, Saudi fighter jet downed
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Houthi attacks have largely emptied Riyadh airport; a missile struck Jeddah, and Yemen says a Saudi F-15 Typhoon was shot down. (Source: Ettelaat (citing Wall Street Journal))

item.title: Macron heads to the Gulf to address Hormuz crisis
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: French President Macron will visit Kuwait, UAE, Bahrain, and Qatar on October 19–21 to discuss the Strait of Hormuz and the energy crisis. (Source: IRNA (citing Reuters))

item.title: Fed raises rates: The cost of the Iran war reaches the American consumer
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The U.S. Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023, citing inflation driven by the Iran war; Trump opposed the move. (Source: Kayhan)

item.title: Flooding in Istanbul: Schools closed, public workers granted leave
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Heavy rain brought flooding to Istanbul; schools closed, administrative leave granted to public workers, residents urged to stay home. (Source: ISNA)

item.title: School hijab ban in Azerbaijan sparks protests spilling into Turkey
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: A ban on headscarves and veiled teachers in Azerbaijani schools has widened into a diplomatic rift; protests erupted in Istanbul. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: IMF forecasts 7.6% contraction for Iran in 2026; Tehran's own data looks worse
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: The IMF projected Iran's economy will shrink 7.6% in 2026 due to war effects; Tehran's own statistics show a 10.1% decline. (Source: Kayhan)

item.title: Huthis strike Aramco in Dhahran: headquarters evacuated
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Saudi Arabia's Energy Ministry confirmed a missile strike on Aramco's Dhahran administrative building; four people wounded in Riyadh. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: 77 U.S. lawmakers press for disclosure on civilian deaths in Iran war
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Seventy-seven U.S. Congress members sent a letter demanding official disclosure from the Pentagon about civilian deaths in the war with Iran. (Source: IRNA)

item.title: Amnesty International: wave of executions sweeping Iran's protest crackdown
item.dc:creator: AI Agent
item.description: Amnesty International reported five executions linked to the Dey uprising; same day, an appeals court upheld execution of political prisoner. (Source: Iran International)
